title: Generative AI cost control runbook
summary: Use billing evidence to identify, contain, and verify generative AI cost reductions without making unsupported savings claims. The playbook includes remediation paths for missing data, failed controls, and unacceptable quality changes.
prerequisites: Access to authoritative billing and usage records for the service being reviewed
A named owner who can approve or reverse operational changes
A documented quality or service boundary that cost reductions must preserve

sections.title: Immediate cost-control path
paragraphs: To control generative AI cost, establish a billing baseline, rank the largest attributable cost contributors, apply one reversible control at a time, and accept a saving only when complete billing evidence confirms it without violating the documented quality or service boundary. This is an intermediate-level playbook for practitioners who already have access to service ownership and billing records.

Step 1: Define the service, owner, accounting boundary, comparison period, and quality or service boundary before changing anything. If ownership or scope cannot be established, stop the change, assign an accountable owner, and record the proposed saving as UNKNOWN until the boundary is agreed.

Step 2: Build a baseline from the authoritative billing and usage records, keeping different currencies, accounting periods, and incompatible usage measures separate. If records are missing or delayed, request the missing access or export, mark the affected amount UNKNOWN, and do not use partial data to claim a saving.

Step 3: Rank cost contributors using dimensions actually present in the billing evidence, such as workload, service, project, or accountable owner. If a charge cannot be attributed, place it in an unattributed category, assign someone to investigate it, and do not infer an owner or workload from unsupported clues.

Step 4: Select a control that is reversible and narrow enough to measure, then document its owner, start time, rollback condition, and expected evidence. If approval or rollback authority is unavailable, do not apply the control; use monitoring and notification while the required authority is obtained.

sections.title: Apply controls and review the source correction
paragraphs: Step 5: Test the selected control against representative work while measuring both cost evidence and the documented quality or service boundary. If representative work is unavailable, run an approved controlled sample or defer the change; do not generalize from an unrepresentative test.

Step 6: Expand the control gradually only while the measured boundary remains acceptable. If quality or service performance crosses the rollback condition, reverse the change, preserve the evidence, and investigate before attempting another control.

Step 7: Compare complete post-change billing records with the defined baseline using the same accounting boundary and compatible periods. If the periods or measures are not comparable, correct the comparison or wait for complete records; report the saving as UNKNOWN until a valid comparison exists.

sections.callout: Never present an estimated or incomplete reduction as an established saving. Record it as UNKNOWN until comparable billing evidence is complete.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Expected evidence consists of the defined accounting boundary, the authoritative baseline records, a ranked view of attributable and unattributed costs, the selected control and approval, test results, rollback conditions, and complete post-change billing records. Each record should identify its period and accountable owner so another reviewer can reproduce the decision.

Verify the result by confirming that baseline and post-change records use the same boundary, compatible periods, and compatible measures; that unattributed or missing amounts remain explicitly UNKNOWN; and that the documented quality or service boundary remained acceptable. If any check fails, withdraw the savings claim, restore the last acceptable control state when necessary, correct or obtain the missing evidence, and repeat the verification.

The runbook succeeded only when a reviewer can trace the decision from source billing records through the applied control to a reproducible result. If that trace cannot be reproduced, treat the result as unverified and keep the claimed saving UNKNOWN.
